records.source: וְהָרָעָ֖ב כָּבֵ֥ד בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And the famine [was] heavy in the land.
pieces: Meanwhile the famine lay heavy on the land.

L.1: And the famine was heavy in the land.

R.1: The famine in Canaan was still very bad.

decisions.choice: heavy: severe
decisions.reason: Kaved, "heavy", describes a famine that weighs on the land (12:10; 41:31). The drought did not let up.

decisions.choice: in Canaan
decisions.reason: Readable names the land, Canaan, where Jacob's family lived.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר כִּלּוּ֙ לֶאֱכֹ֣ל אֶת־הַשֶּׁ֔בֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵבִ֖יאוּ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ אֲבִיהֶ֔ם שֻׁ֖בוּ שִׁבְרוּ־לָ֥נוּ מְעַט־אֹֽכֶל׃
records.gloss: And it was, when they had finished eating the grain which they had brought from Egypt, and said to them their father, go back, buy for us a little food.
pieces: Once the grain they had brought back from Egypt was all eaten, their father told them, "Go back again and get us a little food."

L.2: And it happened, when they had finished eating the grain that they had brought from Egypt, that their father said to them, "Go back, buy us a little food."

R.2: When the family had eaten all the grain the brothers had brought from Egypt, their father said, "Go to Egypt again. Buy some more food for us."

decisions.choice: a little food: Jacob avoids the hard question
decisions.reason: Jacob speaks as if buying "a little food" were simple. He says nothing of Simeon in prison or of the man's demand for Benjamin (42:20), which Judah must now raise.

records.source: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלָ֛יו יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר הָעֵ֣ד הֵעִד֩ בָּ֨נוּ הָאִ֤ישׁ לֵאמֹר֙ לֹֽא־תִרְא֣וּ פָנַ֔י בִּלְתִּ֖י אֲחִיכֶ֥ם אִתְּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And said to him Judah, saying, solemnly warned us the man, saying, not will you see my face unless your brother [is] with you.
pieces: Judah answered him, "The man warned us in the strongest terms, 'Do not show yourselves before me unless your brother comes with you.'

L.3: But Judah said to him, "The man solemnly warned us, saying, 'You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.'

R.3: Judah answered, "The man gave us a strong warning. He said, 'You will not get in to see me unless your brother is with you.'

decisions.choice: solemnly warned: the verb doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: "He warned, he warned us": the doubled verb stresses how seriously the man meant it. The verb (he'id) is used of a warning given before witnesses.

decisions.choice: see my face: be admitted to my presence
decisions.reason: To see a ruler's face is to come before him (44:23). Without Benjamin they could not even ask to buy grain.

decisions.choice: Judah speaks: the brother who will lead
decisions.reason: Reuben's offer failed (42:37-38). From here on Judah takes the lead, as he will in his great speech (44:18-34).

records.source: אִם־יֶשְׁךָ֛ מְשַׁלֵּ֥חַ אֶת־אָחִ֖ינוּ אִתָּ֑נוּ נֵרְדָ֕ה וְנִשְׁבְּרָ֥ה לְךָ֖ אֹֽכֶל׃
records.gloss: If you are sending our brother with us, we will go down and buy for you food.
pieces: Let our brother come with us, and we will go down and get food for you.

L.4: If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy you food.

R.4: If you let our brother go with us, we will go and buy food for you.

records.source: וְאִם־אֵינְךָ֥ מְשַׁלֵּ֖חַ לֹ֣א נֵרֵ֑ד כִּֽי־הָאִ֞ישׁ אָמַ֤ר אֵלֵ֨ינוּ֙ לֹֽא־תִרְא֣וּ פָנַ֔י בִּלְתִּ֖י אֲחִיכֶ֥ם אִתְּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: But if not you are sending, not will we go down, for the man said to us, not will you see my face unless your brother [is] with you.
pieces: But if you refuse to send him, we will not go, for the man's words to us were, 'Unless your brother is with you, you will not see my face.'"

L.5: But if you will not send [him], we will not go down, for the man said to us, 'You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.'"

R.5: But if you will not let him go, we will not go either. The man told us, 'You will not get in to see me unless your brother is with you.'"

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָמָ֥ה הֲרֵעֹתֶ֖ם לִ֑י לְהַגִּ֣יד לָאִ֔ישׁ הַע֥וֹד לָכֶ֖ם אָֽח׃
records.gloss: And said Israel, why did you do harm to me by telling the man [that you] still [had] a brother?
pieces: Israel said, "Why did you do me such harm? Why did you have to tell the man there was another brother?"

L.6: And Israel said, "Why did you treat me so badly by telling the man that you had another brother?"

R.6: Israel said, "You have hurt me! Why did you tell the man that you had another brother?"

decisions.choice: Israel: Jacob as head of the family
decisions.reason: In this chapter the narrator calls the father "Israel" (verses 6, 8, 11), the name God gave him (32:28; 35:10), as he makes the decision that will carry the family into Egypt.

decisions.choice: do harm to me: treat me badly
decisions.reason: Hera'otem is from ra, "evil, harm". Jacob feels wronged, though his sons only answered questions.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֡וּ שָׁא֣וֹל שָֽׁאַל־הָ֠אִישׁ לָ֣נוּ וּלְמֽוֹלַדְתֵּ֜נוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר הַע֨וֹד אֲבִיכֶ֥ם חַי֙ הֲיֵ֣שׁ לָכֶ֣ם אָ֔ח וַנַ֨גֶּד־ל֔וֹעַל־פִּ֖י הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה הֲיָד֣וֹעַ נֵדַ֔ע כִּ֣י יֹאמַ֔ר הוֹרִ֖ידוּ אֶת־אֲחִיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they said, expressly asked the man about us and about our kindred, saying, is still your father alive? Is there to you a brother? And we told him according to these words. Could we possibly know that he would say, bring down your brother?
pieces: They said, "The man pressed us with questions about ourselves and our relatives: 'Is your father still alive? Have you a brother?' All we did was answer what he asked. How could we have guessed he would tell us, 'Bring your brother down'?"

L.7: And they said, "The man questioned [us] closely about ourselves and our family, saying, 'Is your father still alive? Do you have a brother?' And we answered him according to these words. Could we possibly have known that he would say, 'Bring your brother down'?"

R.7: They answered, "The man asked us a lot of questions about our family. He asked, 'Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?' We only told him what he asked. How could we know he would tell us to bring our brother to Egypt?"

decisions.choice: expressly asked: the verb doubled
decisions.reason: "Asking, he asked": the man questioned them closely.

decisions.choice: the brothers' account and chapter 42
alternatives: the brothers shade the story to excuse themselves
decisions.reason: In chapter 42 the brothers offer the news of their father and youngest brother in their own defense (42:13); the questions are not recorded there. Judah repeats this account to Joseph himself (44:19), so the narrator may simply have told the first meeting briefly.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוּדָ֜ה אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אָבִ֗יו שִׁלְחָ֥ה הַנַּ֛עַר אִתִּ֖י וְנָק֣וּמָה וְנֵלֵ֑כָה וְנִֽחְיֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א נָמ֔וּת גַּם־אֲנַ֥חְנוּ גַם־אַתָּ֖ה גַּם־טַפֵּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Judah to Israel his father, send the boy with me, and we will arise and go, that we may live and not die, both we and you and our little ones.
pieces: Judah said to his father Israel, "Send the boy with me, and let us set out now. Then we will stay alive and not die, all of us: we, you and our little ones.

L.8: And Judah said to Israel his father, "Send the boy with me, and let us arise and go, so that we may live and not die, both we and you and our little ones.

R.8: Then Judah said to his father, "Send the boy with me. Let us go now. Then we will all stay alive: you, we and our children. If we do not go, we will die.

decisions.choice: the boy: Benjamin, the youngest
decisions.reason: Na'ar can mean a boy or a young man. Benjamin was by now a grown man (46:21 lists ten sons), but to the family he is still "the boy", the youngest and most protected.

decisions.choice: that we may live and not die: Jacob's own words
decisions.reason: Judah answers his father with the words Jacob used when he first sent them to Egypt (42:2).

records.source: אָֽנֹכִי֙ אֶֽעֶרְבֶ֔נּוּ מִיָּדִ֖י תְּבַקְשֶׁ֑נּוּ אִם־לֹ֨א הֲבִיאֹתִ֤יו אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ וְהִצַּגְתִּ֣יו לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְחָטָ֥אתִֽי לְךָ֖ כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: I, I will be surety for him; from my hand you may require him. If not I bring him to you and set him before you, then I will bear blame to you all the days.
pieces: I pledge myself for him. Demand him back from me. If I fail to bring him home and stand him before your eyes, the guilt will be mine before you as long as I live.

L.9: I myself will be surety for him; from my hand you may require him. If I do not bring him [back] to you and set him before you, then I will bear the blame before you all my days.

R.9: I promise to keep him safe. You can make me pay if anything happens to him. If I do not bring him back to you, you can blame me for the rest of my life.

decisions.choice: be surety for him: pledge oneself for another
decisions.reason: Arav means to stand as a guarantee for someone, answering with oneself for his safety (44:32).

decisions.choice: Judah offers himself, not his sons
decisions.reason: Reuben offered his sons' lives (42:37); Judah offers his own. The brother who proposed selling Joseph (37:26-27) now stakes himself on Rachel's other son, and he keeps his word (44:33).

decisions.choice: I will bear the blame: literally "I will have sinned"
decisions.reason: Chata, "to sin", here means to stand guilty and answerable, as in 44:32.

records.source: כִּ֖י לוּלֵ֣א הִתְמַהְמָ֑הְנוּ כִּֽי־עַתָּ֥ה שַׁ֖בְנוּ זֶ֥ה פַעֲמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: For if we had not delayed, surely by now we would have returned this twice.
pieces: If we had not wasted all this time, we could have been there and back twice by now."

L.10: For if we had not delayed, surely by now we could have returned twice."

R.10: If we had not waited so long, we could have gone to Egypt and come back two times by now."

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אֲבִיהֶ֗ם אִם־כֵּ֣ן׀אֵפוֹא֮ זֹ֣את עֲשׂוּ֒ קְח֞וּ מִזִּמְרַ֤ת הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ בִּכְלֵיכֶ֔ם וְהוֹרִ֥ידוּ לָאִ֖ישׁ מִנְחָ֑ה מְעַ֤ט צֳרִי֙ וּמְעַ֣ט דְּבַ֔שׁ נְכֹ֣את וָלֹ֔ט בָּטְנִ֖ים וּשְׁקֵדִֽים׃
records.gloss: And said to them Israel their father, if so, then, this do: take of [the] best produce of the land in your vessels, and carry down to the man a gift, a little balm and a little honey, gum and myrrh, pistachio nuts and almonds.
pieces: Their father Israel told them, "Since there is no other way, here is what you must do. Pack some of the choicest things our land produces and take them down to the man as a gift: a little balm and a little honey, gum and resin, pistachios and almonds.

L.11: Then their father Israel said to them, "If it must be so, then do this: take some of the best produce of the land in your containers, and carry down a gift to the man: a little balm and a little honey, gum and myrrh, pistachio nuts and almonds.

R.11: Then their father Israel said to them, "If it has to be this way, then do this. Take some of the best things that grow in our land. Take them to the man as a gift: some balm, some honey, some spices, and some pistachio nuts and almonds.

decisions.choice: the best products of the land
alternatives: the song of the land (what it is praised for)
decisions.reason: Zimrah is used only here in this sense; it seems to mean the choice produce for which the land is famous. Because the same letters spell a word for "song", some read it as "what the land is praised for".

decisions.choice: a gift: a present to win favor
decisions.reason: Minchah is a gift brought to a superior to show respect and gain his goodwill. Jacob sent such a gift ahead to Esau (32:13, 20).

decisions.choice: balm, gum and myrrh: the goods of the caravan
decisions.reason: These are the same goods the Ishmaelite traders were carrying to Egypt when the brothers sold Joseph to them (37:25). Honey may be bees' honey or a thick syrup made from dates or grapes. Even in famine, Canaan's resins and nuts were luxuries Egypt did not grow.

decisions.choice: gum and resin
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the same words for these resins as in 37:25; the exact plants are uncertain.

decisions.choice: some spices
decisions.reason: Readable uses one general word for the aromatic resins.

records.source: וְכֶ֥סֶף מִשְׁנֶ֖ה קְח֣וּ בְיֶדְכֶ֑ם וְאֶת־הַכֶּ֜סֶף הַמּוּשָׁ֨ב בְּפִ֤י אַמְתְּחֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ תָּשִׁ֣יבוּ בְיֶדְכֶ֔ם אוּלַ֥י מִשְׁגֶּ֖ה הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And silver double take in your hand, and the silver returned in [the] mouth of your sacks take back in your hand; perhaps it [was] a mistake.
pieces: Carry twice the money with you, and give back the money you found at the top of your sacks; it may have been an oversight.

L.12: And take double the silver in your hand, and carry back in your hand the silver that was returned in the mouth of your sacks. Perhaps it was a mistake.

R.12: Take twice as much money with you. Take back the money that was put in your bags. Maybe someone made a mistake.

decisions.choice: double silver: twice the amount
decisions.reason: Mishneh means double or a second portion. They are to take enough to pay for new grain and to repay the silver that came back (verses 21-22).

decisions.choice: money
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "silver"; Balanced and Readable say "money", as in chapters 42 and 44.

records.source: וְאֶת־אֲחִיכֶ֖ם קָ֑חוּ וְק֖וּמוּ שׁ֥וּבוּ אֶל־הָאִֽישׁ׃
records.gloss: And your brother take, and arise, go back to the man.
pieces: Take your brother as well. Get up and return to the man.

L.13: And take your brother, and arise, go back to the man.

R.13: Take your brother and go back to the man.

records.source: וְאֵ֣ל שַׁדַּ֗י יִתֵּ֨ן לָכֶ֤ם רַחֲמִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָאִ֔ישׁ וְשִׁלַּ֥ח לָכֶ֛ם אֶת־אֲחִיכֶ֥ם אַחֵ֖ר וְאֶת־בִּנְיָמִ֑ין וַאֲנִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁכֹ֖לְתִּי שָׁכָֽלְתִּי׃
records.gloss: And God Almighty give you compassion before the man, that he may release to you your brother, other, and Benjamin. And I, as I am bereaved, I am bereaved.
pieces: May God Almighty stir the man's heart to mercy toward you, so that he releases your other brother to you, and Benjamin too. As for me, if I must lose my children, then I lose them."

L.14: And may God Almighty give you compassion before the man, so that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved."

R.14: I pray that God Almighty will make the man kind to you. Then he will let Simeon and Benjamin come home with you. If I lose my children, then I lose them."

decisions.choice: God Almighty: El Shaddai
decisions.reason: El Shaddai is the name under which God promised Abraham and Jacob descendants (17:1; 28:3; 35:11). Jacob calls on the God of the promise to protect the sons of the promise.

decisions.choice: compassion: tender mercy
decisions.reason: Rachamim is deep, tender compassion. Jacob prays that the man will feel it, and in verse 30 the same word describes what Joseph feels on seeing Benjamin.

decisions.choice: as I am bereaved, I am bereaved: resignation
decisions.reason: A way of accepting what cannot be avoided: if I lose them, I lose them (compare Esther 4:16).

decisions.choice: Simeon
decisions.reason: Readable names the brother held in Egypt (42:24).

records.source: וַיִּקְח֤וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את וּמִשְׁנֶה־כֶּ֛סֶף לָקְח֥וּ בְיָדָ֖ם וְאֶת־בִּנְיָמִ֑ן וַיָּקֻ֨מוּ֙ וַיֵּרְד֣וּ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיַּֽעַמְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י יוֹסֵֽף׃
records.gloss: And took the men this gift, and double silver they took in their hand, and Benjamin, and they arose and went down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.
pieces: The men took the gift, took twice the money, and took Benjamin. Then they set off down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.

L.15: So the men took this gift, and they took double the silver in their hand, and Benjamin. And they arose and went down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.

R.15: So the brothers took the gifts, twice as much money, and Benjamin. They went down to Egypt and came to Joseph.

records.source: וַיַּ֨רְא יוֹסֵ֣ף אִתָּם֮ אֶת־בִּנְיָמִין֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לַֽאֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־בֵּית֔וֹ הָבֵ֥א אֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים הַבָּ֑יְתָה וּטְבֹ֤חַ טֶ֨בַח֙ וְהָכֵ֔ן כִּ֥י אִתִּ֛י יֹאכְל֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים בַּֽצָּהֳרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And saw Joseph with them Benjamin, and he said to [the one] who [was] over his house, bring the men to the house, and slaughter a slaughter and prepare [it], for with me will eat the men at noon.
pieces: As soon as Joseph saw Benjamin among them, he told the man in charge of his household, "Bring these men into the house. Have an animal butchered and a meal made ready; they will be dining with me at noon."

L.16: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the [man] who [was] over his house, "Bring the men into the house, and slaughter an animal and prepare [it], for the men will eat with me at noon."

R.16: Joseph saw that Benjamin was with them. He said to the servant in charge of his house, "Take these men to my house. Kill an animal and cook it. These men will eat with me at noon."

decisions.choice: the one over his house: Joseph's steward
decisions.reason: The man "over the house" managed a great household, as Joseph once did for Potiphar (39:4-5).

decisions.choice: slaughter an animal: a feast with meat
decisions.reason: Meat was eaten on special occasions. Joseph orders a feast in honor of his guests.

decisions.choice: at noon: the main meal of the day
decisions.reason: Tsohorayim, "noon", was the time of the principal meal in Egypt.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ הָאִ֔ישׁ כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֣ר יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיָּבֵ֥א הָאִ֛ישׁ אֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים בֵּ֥יתָה יוֹסֵֽף׃
records.gloss: And did the man as said Joseph, and brought the man the men to [the] house of Joseph.
pieces: The steward carried out Joseph's orders and led the brothers into Joseph's house.

L.17: And the man did as Joseph said, and the man brought the men into Joseph's house.

R.17: The servant did what Joseph said. He took the brothers to Joseph's house.

records.source: וַיִּֽירְא֣וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֗ים כִּ֣י הֽוּבְאוּ֮ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵף֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ עַל־דְּבַ֤ר הַכֶּ֨סֶף֙ הַשָּׁ֤ב בְּאַמְתְּחֹתֵ֨ינוּ֙ בַּתְּחִלָּ֔ה אֲנַ֖חְנוּ מֽוּבָאִ֑ים לְהִתְגֹּלֵ֤ל עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙ וּלְהִתְנַפֵּ֣ל עָלֵ֔ינוּ וְלָקַ֧חַת אֹתָ֛נוּ לַעֲבָדִ֖ים וְאֶת־חֲמֹרֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And were afraid the men because they were brought [to the] house of Joseph, and they said, on account of the silver that returned in our sacks at the beginning we are being brought, to roll himself on us and to throw himself on us and to take us as slaves, and our donkeys.
pieces: Being taken into Joseph's house terrified the men. They said to themselves, "This is about the money that turned up in our sacks last time. He has brought us in here to turn on us and fall on us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys."

L.18: And the men were afraid because they were brought into Joseph's house, and they said, "It is because of the silver that was returned in our sacks the first time that we are being brought in, so that he can roll himself upon us and fall upon us, and take us as slaves, along with our donkeys."

R.18: The brothers were afraid because they were taken to Joseph's house. They said to each other, "It is about the money we found in our bags last time. That is why we were brought here. He is going to jump on us and make us his slaves. He will take our donkeys too."

decisions.choice: roll himself upon us: attack us
decisions.reason: The verb (hitgolel) occurs only here with this sense. It seems to picture someone rolling down on a victim, an attack or a trumped-up charge.

decisions.choice: take us as slaves: the brothers fear what they did to Joseph
decisions.reason: The brothers who sold Joseph as a slave (37:28) fear becoming slaves themselves.

decisions.choice: said to themselves / said to each other
decisions.reason: They are speaking among themselves, not to the steward; that conversation comes in verse 19.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" at every level: the brothers fear being seized and losing their freedom, as they once sold Joseph (m2), so the style guide keeps the word.

records.source: וַֽיִּגְּשׁוּ֙ אֶל־הָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו פֶּ֥תַח הַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: And they approached the man who [was] over [the] house of Joseph and spoke to him [at the] entrance of the house,
pieces: At the doorway of the house they came up to the man in charge of Joseph's household and spoke to him.

L.19: So they came near to the man who [was] over Joseph's house and spoke to him at the entrance of the house,

R.19: So at the door of the house, they went to the servant in charge of Joseph's house and talked to him.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֑י יָרֹ֥ד יָרַ֛דְנוּ בַּתְּחִלָּ֖ה לִשְׁבָּר־אֹֽכֶל׃
records.gloss: And they said, pardon, my lord, indeed we came down at the beginning to buy food.
pieces: "Excuse us, my lord," they said. "We really did come down here before, just to buy food.

L.20: and they said, "Please, my lord, we did indeed come down the first time to buy food.

R.20: They said, "Please, sir, listen. We came here once before to buy food.

decisions.choice: bi: "please, pardon", a humble opening
decisions.reason: Bi is a polite word used when asking a superior for a hearing (44:18).

decisions.choice: we did indeed come down: the doubled verb
decisions.reason: The doubled verb stresses that their only purpose was to buy food, not to spy or steal.

decisions.choice: sir
decisions.reason: Readable uses "sir", as in chapters 42 and 44.

records.source: וַֽיְהִ֞י כִּי־בָ֣אנוּ אֶל־הַמָּל֗וֹן וַֽנִּפְתְּחָה֙ אֶת־אַמְתְּחֹתֵ֔ינוּ וְהִנֵּ֤ה כֶֽסֶף־אִישׁ֙ בְּפִ֣י אַמְתַּחְתּ֔וֹ כַּסְפֵּ֖נוּ בְּמִשְׁקָל֑וֹ וַנָּ֥שֶׁב אֹת֖וֹ בְּיָדֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And it was, when we came to the lodging place and opened our sacks, and behold, [the] silver of each man [was] in [the] mouth of his sack, our silver in its weight; and we have brought it back in our hand.
pieces: When we reached our night's lodging and opened our sacks, there was each man's money at the top of his sack, the full weight of it. Here it is; we have brought it back.

L.21: And it happened, when we came to the lodging place and opened our sacks, look, each man's silver was in the mouth of his sack, our silver in its full weight. So we have brought it back in our hand.

R.21: But when we stopped for the night and opened our bags, each of us found his money in his bag. All of it was there. So we have brought it back to you.

decisions.choice: in its weight: the full amount
decisions.reason: Silver was weighed out, not counted, so "in its weight" means every bit of it was there.

decisions.choice: the brothers simplify the story
decisions.reason: According to 42:27 and 42:35, one brother found his silver at the lodging place and the rest found theirs at home. Speaking to the steward, the brothers tell it more simply, as if all were found on the road.

records.source: וְכֶ֧סֶף אַחֵ֛ר הוֹרַ֥דְנוּ בְיָדֵ֖נוּ לִשְׁבָּר־אֹ֑כֶל לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְנוּ מִי־שָׂ֥ם כַּסְפֵּ֖נוּ בְּאַמְתְּחֹתֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And silver, other, we have brought down in our hand to buy food. Not do we know who put our silver in our sacks.
pieces: We have brought other money besides, to pay for food this time. Who put our money back in our sacks, we cannot tell."

L.22: And we have brought down other silver in our hand to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our sacks."

R.22: And we have brought other money with us to pay for more food. Someone put our money back in our bags, but we have no idea who did it."

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ שָׁל֨וֹם לָכֶ֜ם אַל־תִּירָ֗אוּ אֱלֹ֨הֵיכֶ֜ם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֤י אֲבִיכֶם֙ נָתַ֨ן לָכֶ֤ם מַטְמוֹן֙ בְּאַמְתְּחֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם כַּסְפְּכֶ֖ם בָּ֣א אֵלָ֑י וַיּוֹצֵ֥א אֲלֵהֶ֖ם אֶת־שִׁמְעֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And he said, peace [be] to you, do not fear; your God and [the] God of your father has given to you hidden treasure in your sacks; your silver came to me. And he brought out to them Simeon.
pieces: "All is well," he replied. "Put away your fear. It was your God, the God of your father, who hid treasure in your sacks for you. Your money reached me." And he led Simeon out to join them.

L.23: And he said, "Peace to you, do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father has given you treasure in your sacks. Your silver came to me." Then he brought Simeon out to them.

R.23: The servant answered, "You are safe. There is nothing to fear. The God your father worships, who is your God too, must have put that treasure in your bags. Your payment reached me." Then he brought Simeon out to the brothers.

decisions.choice: peace to you: all is well
decisions.reason: Shalom lakhem is a greeting and a word of reassurance: you are safe.

decisions.choice: your God has given you treasure: truer than the steward knows
decisions.reason: The steward, who probably knows Joseph's plan, turns aside the brothers' fear by crediting their God. His words are true in a deeper sense: God is at work in all that is happening to them (45:5-8).

decisions.choice: treasure: something hidden away
decisions.reason: Matmon is a hidden store or buried treasure (Job 3:21; Jeremiah 41:8).

decisions.choice: your silver came to me: your payment was received
decisions.reason: The steward assures them that they owe nothing for the first purchase.

records.source: וַיָּבֵ֥א הָאִ֛ישׁ אֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים בֵּ֣יתָה יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיִּתֶּן־מַ֨יִם֙ וַיִּרְחֲצ֣וּ רַגְלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּתֵּ֥ן מִסְפּ֖וֹא לַחֲמֹֽרֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And brought the man the men to [the] house of Joseph, and he gave water, and they washed their feet, and he gave fodder to their donkeys.
pieces: The steward led them inside Joseph's house. He brought water so they could wash their feet, and he gave their donkeys feed.

L.24: And the man brought the men into Joseph's house and gave [them] water, and they washed their feet, and he gave their donkeys fodder.

R.24: The servant led the brothers into Joseph's house. He brought them water, and they washed their feet. He also fed their donkeys.

decisions.choice: water to wash their feet: the welcome of a guest
decisions.reason: Offering water for dusty feet was the first act of hospitality (18:4; 24:32). The brothers are treated as honored guests, not prisoners.

records.source: וַיָּכִ֨ינוּ֙ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֔ה עַד־בּ֥וֹא יוֹסֵ֖ף בַּֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם כִּ֣י שָֽׁמְע֔וּ כִּי־שָׁ֖ם יֹ֥אכְלוּ לָֽחֶם׃
records.gloss: And they prepared the gift until Joseph came at noon, for they had heard that there they would eat bread.
pieces: Then they set out their gift, ready for when Joseph would come at noon, because they had been told they would be eating a meal there.

L.25: And they got the gift ready for Joseph's coming at noon, for they had heard that they would eat bread there.

R.25: They got their gifts ready to give to Joseph when he came at noon. They had heard that they were going to eat there.

decisions.choice: eat a meal / eat
decisions.reason: "Eat bread" means to have a meal.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤א יוֹסֵף֙ הַבַּ֔יְתָה וַיָּבִ֥יאּוּ ל֛וֹ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־בְּיָדָ֖ם הַבָּ֑יְתָה וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ־ל֖וֹ אָֽרְצָה׃
records.gloss: And came Joseph home, and they brought to him the gift which [was] in their hand into the house, and they bowed down to him to [the] ground.
pieces: Joseph came home, and they carried the gift they had with them into the house and presented it to him, bowing low to the ground.

L.26: When Joseph came home, they brought him the gift that was in their hand into the house, and they bowed down to him to the ground.

R.26: Joseph came home, and the brothers handed him the gifts they had carried into the house. Then they bowed low, with their faces to the ground.

decisions.choice: they bowed down to him: now all eleven brothers
decisions.reason: This time Benjamin is with them, and all eleven bow to Joseph, as the eleven stars did in his second dream (37:9).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל לָהֶם֙ לְשָׁל֔וֹם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲשָׁל֛וֹם אֲבִיכֶ֥ם הַזָּקֵ֖ן אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲמַרְתֶּ֑ם הַעוֹדֶ֖נּוּ חָֽי׃
records.gloss: And he asked them about welfare, and he said, is it well [with] your father, the old [man] of whom you spoke? Is he still alive?
pieces: Joseph asked after their health. "And your father, the old man you spoke of," he said, "is he well? Is he still alive?"

L.27: And he asked them about [their] welfare and said, "Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he still alive?"

R.27: Joseph asked them if they were well. Then he said, "You told me about your father, who is an old man. Is he well? Is he still alive?"

decisions.choice: welfare (shalom): health, well-being
decisions.reason: Shalom here is a person's well-being, the ordinary greeting "are you well?" The word recalls 37:4 and 37:14: the brothers could not speak to Joseph with shalom, and Jacob sent him to see about their shalom.

decisions.choice: is he still alive?: Joseph's real question
decisions.reason: Behind the polite inquiry is a son's longing. Joseph asks again when he makes himself known (45:3).

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ שָׁל֛וֹם לְעַבְדְּךָ֥ לְאָבִ֖ינוּ עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ חָ֑י וַֽיִּקְּד֖וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And they said, [it is] well with your servant, our father; still he [is] alive. And they bowed the head and bowed down.
pieces: "Your servant our father is in good health," they answered. "He is still alive." And they bowed their heads and knelt low.

L.28: And they said, "Your servant our father is well; he is still alive." And they bowed their heads and bowed down.

R.28: They answered, "Our father is well. He is still alive." And they bowed down to Joseph again.

decisions.choice: your servant our father: Jacob too bows
decisions.reason: By calling Jacob "your servant", the brothers make their father bow to Joseph in their words, as the sun did in Joseph's dream (37:9-10).

decisions.choice: bowed the head: a gesture of respect
decisions.reason: Qadad is to bow the head, often followed, as here, by bowing to the ground (24:26).

decisions.choice: they bowed down: written form and reading tradition
decisions.reason: The Masoretic scribes note a difference between the written spelling of this verb and the way it is to be read. The difference is only in spelling; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: Our father
decisions.reason: Readable drops the courteous "your servant", as elsewhere.

records.source: וַיִּשָּׂ֣א עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּ֞רְא אֶת־בִּנְיָמִ֣ין אָחִיו֮ בֶּן־אִמּוֹ֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲזֶה֙ אֲחִיכֶ֣ם הַקָּטֹ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֵלָ֑י וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים יָחְנְךָ֖ בְּנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And he lifted his eyes and saw Benjamin his brother, the son of his mother, and said, is this your brother, the youngest, of whom you spoke to me? And he said, God be gracious to you, my son.
pieces: Then Joseph raised his eyes and caught sight of Benjamin, his brother, born of his own mother. "Is this the youngest brother you spoke to me about?" he asked. And he said, "May God show you favor, my son."

L.29: And he lifted up his eyes and saw Benjamin his brother, his mother's son, and said, "Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?" And he said, "May God be gracious to you, my son."

R.29: Then Joseph saw his brother Benjamin. They had the same mother. Joseph asked, "Is this the youngest one, the brother you told me about?" Then he said to Benjamin, "May God be kind to you, my son."

decisions.choice: his mother's son: his full brother
decisions.reason: Benjamin was the only other son of Rachel (35:16-18). The phrase marks the bond Joseph feels.

decisions.choice: God be gracious to you: a blessing
decisions.reason: Chanan means to show favor freely. Jacob spoke of his children as those "God has graciously given" (33:5), and the priestly blessing asks that God be gracious (Numbers 6:25).

decisions.choice: and he said: a pause before the blessing
decisions.reason: The narrator introduces Joseph's words a second time, as though he could not go on at once. "My son" is how an older man of rank might greet a younger one.

decisions.choice: to Benjamin
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the blessing was spoken.

records.source: וַיְמַהֵ֣ר יוֹסֵ֗ף כִּֽי־נִכְמְר֤וּ רַחֲמָיו֙ אֶל־אָחִ֔יו וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לִבְכּ֑וֹת וַיָּבֹ֥א הַחַ֖דְרָה וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ שָֽׁמָּה׃
records.gloss: And hurried Joseph, for were stirred his compassion toward his brother, and he sought to weep, and he went into the inner room and wept there.
pieces: Joseph had to leave quickly; his heart was so stirred for his brother that he was close to tears. He went into an inner room, and there he wept.

L.30: Then Joseph hurried [out], for his compassion grew warm toward his brother, and he looked for [a place] to weep. And he went into the inner room and wept there.

R.30: Joseph loved his brother so much that he was about to cry. He hurried out of the room and went to his own room. There he cried.

decisions.choice: his compassion grew warm: deep feeling welled up
decisions.reason: Literally his "compassions" (rachamim, the inner parts, felt as the seat of tender love) grew hot. The same is said of the mother in 1 Kings 3:26.

decisions.choice: compassion: Jacob's prayer answered
decisions.reason: Jacob prayed that God would give his sons compassion (rachamim) before the man (verse 14). The man himself is overcome with it.

decisions.choice: the inner room: a private chamber
decisions.reason: Cheder is an inner or private room, away from the public rooms of the house.

records.source: וַיִּרְחַ֥ץ פָּנָ֖יו וַיֵּצֵ֑א וַיִּ֨תְאַפַּ֔ק וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שִׂ֥ימוּ לָֽחֶם׃
records.gloss: And he washed his face and came out, and he restrained himself and said, set out food.
pieces: Then he washed his face and came out again. Holding his feelings in check, he gave the order: "Bring in the food."

L.31: Then he washed his face and came out; and he controlled himself and said, "Set out the food."

R.31: Then he washed his face and came back out. He made himself stop crying. Then he said, "Bring in the food."

decisions.choice: restrained himself: held in his feelings
decisions.reason: Hit'appeq means to control oneself. In 45:1 Joseph can no longer do so.

records.source: וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ ל֛וֹ לְבַדּ֖וֹ וְלָהֶ֣ם לְבַדָּ֑ם וְלַמִּצְרִ֞ים הָאֹכְלִ֤ים אִתּוֹ֙ לְבַדָּ֔ם כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יוּכְל֜וּן הַמִּצְרִ֗ים לֶאֱכֹ֤ל אֶת־הָֽעִבְרִים֙ לֶ֔חֶם כִּי־תוֹעֵבָ֥ה הִ֖וא לְמִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And they set for him by himself and for them by themselves and for the Egyptians eating with him by themselves, for not are able the Egyptians to eat with the Hebrews bread, for an abomination it [is] to Egypt.
pieces: Food was set out for Joseph by himself, for the brothers by themselves, and for the Egyptians who dined with him by themselves. Egyptians would not share a meal with Hebrews, since they found that abhorrent.

L.32: And they set [food] for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves, because the Egyptians could not eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to Egypt.

R.32: The servants served Joseph at his own table. They served the brothers at another table, and the Egyptians who were eating with Joseph at another. Egyptians would not eat with Hebrews. They thought it was a shameful thing to do.

decisions.choice: abomination: something abhorrent
decisions.reason: To'evah is what a group finds loathsome, here by Egyptian custom. The word is later used for what is abhorrent to God (Leviticus 18:22; Deuteronomy 7:25). Egyptians also looked down on shepherds (46:34).

decisions.choice: three tables: rank and custom
decisions.reason: Joseph eats alone, as befits his high rank, and so keeps his disguise. The Egyptians eat apart from the foreigners, and the Hebrews by themselves.

records.source: וַיֵּשְׁב֣וּ לְפָנָ֔יו הַבְּכֹר֙ כִּבְכֹ֣רָת֔וֹ וְהַצָּעִ֖יר כִּצְעִרָת֑וֹ וַיִּתְמְה֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אִ֥ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth; and looked in astonishment the men each at his neighbor.
pieces: They were seated facing him, the eldest in the place his birthright gave him and the youngest in the place that fit his youth, and the men stared at one another in amazement.

L.33: And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth, and the men looked at one another in amazement.

R.33: The brothers were given seats facing Joseph, from the oldest down to the youngest, each in his place by age. They stared at one another in surprise. How could anyone in Egypt know how old each of them was?

decisions.choice: they looked at one another in amazement: how could he know?
decisions.reason: The brothers were seated in exact order of birth, though nobody had asked their ages. To them it seemed uncanny, as if the Egyptian could read secrets (compare 44:15).

decisions.choice: according to his birthright: by order of birth
decisions.reason: Bekhorah is the right of the firstborn. The seating follows the brothers' birth order, eldest to youngest.

decisions.choice: How could anyone in Egypt know how old each of them was?
decisions.reason: Readable states the reason for their amazement, which the context makes plain.

records.source: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א מַשְׂאֹ֜ת מֵאֵ֣ת פָּנָיו֮ אֲלֵהֶם֒ וַתֵּ֜רֶב מַשְׂאַ֧ת בִּנְיָמִ֛ן מִמַּשְׂאֹ֥ת כֻּלָּ֖ם חָמֵ֣שׁ יָד֑וֹת וַיִּשְׁתּ֥וּ וַֽיִּשְׁכְּר֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And were carried portions from before him to them, and was greater [the] portion of Benjamin than [the] portions of all of them [by] five hands. And they drank and became drunk with him.
pieces: Dishes were sent to them from the food in front of Joseph, and Benjamin got five times as much as any of the others. They drank with him until they were merry.

L.34: And portions were carried to them from before him, and Benjamin's portion was five times greater than the portions of any of them. And they drank and became merry with him.

R.34: Food from Joseph's own table was taken to the brothers. But Benjamin got five times more than any of his brothers. The brothers ate and drank with Joseph and had a good time.

decisions.choice: portions from before him: a mark of honor
decisions.reason: A host honored guests by sending them food from his own table (compare 1 Samuel 9:23-24).

decisions.choice: Benjamin's portion five times larger: a test
decisions.reason: "Five hands" means five times as much. Joseph openly favors Rachel's son, as Jacob once favored Joseph (37:3-4). Will the brothers resent Benjamin as they resented him? Their reaction in chapter 44 gives the answer.

decisions.choice: became drunk: drank freely, were merry
decisions.reason: Shakar can mean to drink one's fill and be merry as well as to be drunk (Haggai 1:6; Song of Songs 5:1). For the first time in the story the brothers relax.
